advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Surface the probe `error` distinctly (e.g. a `degraded`/`error` state in the health field) so a resolution fault is not indistinguishable from pinning-not-configured.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:337: `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001` sets `status["expected"] = False` and `status["error"] = str(exc)`
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:347: `return bool(status.get("bound") and status.get("expected") and not status.get("matched"))` — never consults `error`
ABSENCE: no test covers a resolution fault (e.g. a malformed keyring that is not RemovedInputError); the `error` field is set but never surfaced as a distinct health signal
advisory.finding: opcert_signing_status catches any non-RemovedInputError as `expected:False` (recording an `error` key), but opcert_signer_degraded only checks bound/expected/matched and never inspects `error`. A genuine resolution fault (e.g. keyring load/parse failure) is therefore reported as not-degraded and the /health `opcert` field looks clean — the probe cannot distinguish 'pinning not configured' from 'probe failed to run'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the guard resolution in a best-effort try/except (log-and-return) so a resolver fault can never abort mint_opcert_record, matching the 'never refuses' contract.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:347: `_warn_if_verify_cannot_resolve(tracker, key_path, principal)` is called with no surrounding try/except
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:295-304: the helper calls `_read_opcert_pub` and `_opcert_own_public_keys` with no guard, then logs
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:353: the startup sibling `run_startup_opcert_check` explicitly wraps its resolution in try/except so it 'NEVER raises' — the mint helper does not have the equivalent guard
advisory.finding: _warn_if_verify_cannot_resolve is invoked unwrapped inside mint_opcert_record; despite the docstring's 'purely ADDITIVE: it logs, it never refuses' claim, any unexpected exception raised by _read_opcert_pub or _opcert_own_public_keys would propagate out of the helper and abort minting — a behavior change to the sign path that previously did not call this resolver.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the body of _warn_if_verify_cannot_resolve (or its call site) in try/except Exception that logs at debug and returns, mirroring run_startup_opcert_check.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting `opcert_signing_status`/`run_startup_opcert_check` re-raise `RemovedInputError` (e.g. monkeypatch `load_trusted_environments` to raise it) instead of reporting `expected: False`.
evidence: Named violating input: with `_write_trusted_env` set up, monkeypatch `rebar.attest.trusted_env.load_trusted_environments` to raise `RemovedInputError(...)`; `opcert_signing_status(_Signer(...), repo_root=str(store))` must re-raise rather than return `expected: False`.

Sibling precedent tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py:200 `with pytest.raises(RemovedInputError): store_status()` whose docstring at :186-188 states the test 'is what stops a future widening of that handler from silently swallowing it'.
ABSENCE: search for `RemovedInputError` in the new test file returned no matches.
advisory.finding: The added `except RemovedInputError: raise` contract in `opcert_signing_status` and `run_startup_opcert_check` has no regression test — a future widening of the broad `except Exception` handler to `except BaseException` would silently swallow a removed-but-still-set load-bearing input, and no test would catch it. The sibling `store_status` explicitly guards this exact contract with `test_a_removed_load_bearing_input_fails_hard_instead_of_being_reported`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a malformed/faulting `trusted_environments.yaml` makes `opcert_signing_status` return `expected: False` with an `error` field and never raise.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:337-339 (added) `except Exception as exc: status['expected'] = False; status['error'] = str(exc)`
Docstring claim src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:312-313: 'a malformed config or any resolution fault is reported as expected: False rather than aborting the probe'

Named violating input: write a malformed `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml` (e.g. invalid YAML) so `load_trusted_environments`/`trusted_env_keyring` raises, then assert `opcert_signing_status(signer, repo_root=str(store))` returns `{'expected': False, 'error': ...}` and does NOT raise.
ABSENCE: search for `error` in the new test file returned no matches; no test exercises the swallow path.
advisory.finding: The added generic-fault branch `except Exception as exc: status['expected'] = False; status['error'] = str(exc)` in `opcert_signing_status` is untested — the docstring's promise that 'a malformed config or any resolution fault is reported as expected: False rather than aborting the probe' (and the `error` field it sets) has no test driving it.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize signer_pub and pinned public_keys to the type+base64 body (drop comment) before the `matched` comparison so the probe matches actual verify semantics.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:329: `pinned = [ k.get("public_key") for k in (keyring or []) ...]`
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:332: `status["matched"] = signer_pub is not None and signer_pub in pinned`
src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:84: `f"{principal} {key_line.strip()}" for key_line in keys ...` — verify normalizes via OpenSSH allowed_signers which matches on key body, not the trailing comment
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:265: `_read_opcert_pub` returns the full `.pub` line text including any comment
blocking.finding: opcert_signing_status computes `matched` via exact-string membership of the full .pub line (comment included) in the pinned public_keys, but the real verify path (allowed_signers_from_keys/registry.verify) matches keys on type+base64 body and ignores the comment. A signer whose .pub carries a different comment than the pinned config entry will report matched:False and trigger a spurious DEGRADED warning even though verify_signature would certify it.
blocking.suggested_fix: Compare on `" ".join(line.split()[:2])` (type+key body) for both signer_pub and each pinned key rather than the raw full line.
